2027-01-19.title: Tuesday after the Second Sunday after Denho · Second Day of the Fast of the Ninevites · Mar Macarios
2027-01-19.alt: Season of Denho. Moonnu Nombu, the fast of the Ninevites (Baooutho d'Ninwoye). Commemoration of Mar Macarios the Great of Egypt; name day of Geevarghese Mar Makarios. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-19.verse: Keep awake therefore, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.
theo: On the second day, Jonah finally obeys. He walks a day's journey into the great city and cries his short message. “And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth.” The king's decree is remarkable: “All shall turn from their evil ways and from the violence that is in their hands. Who knows? God may relent.” Fasting without turning from violence and evil would mean nothing. Nineveh fasted with its hands as well as its stomach.

Jesus warns that his coming will be like the days of Noah: people “were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage” and did not notice until the flood came. “Keep awake therefore.” Paul tells us how the watchful live: “Let love be genuine; hate what is evil, hold fast to what is good… Rejoice in hope, be patient in suffering, persevere in prayer.” Today we remember Mar Macarios the Great, the monk of the Egyptian desert, whose watchful prayer and gentleness made him a father to many.
outline: Ask: what would you change if you knew Christ would come tonight?
live: Put right one injustice or harsh word today.
Pray the evening prayer of the Church with your family.
2027-01-19.prayer: Lord God, the people of Nineveh believed you and turned from violence and evil. Keep us awake for the coming of your Son, make our love genuine, and through the prayers of Mar Macarios keep us steadfast in the true faith. Amen.
altar: Every Holy Qurbono looks forward to the coming of the Lord: we keep awake at the altar, awaiting him who comes.

quick: Nineveh fasted and turned from violence and evil.
Keep awake, for the Lord comes unexpectedly.
Let love be genuine; persevere in prayer.
2027-01-19.action: Put right one injustice or harsh word today.
2027-01-19.question: Is my fasting also a turning from evil?

family.explain: The king of Nineveh told everyone to stop doing bad things and pray. God saw that they changed, and he forgave them.
family.intention: We pray that our homes may be places of peace, without harsh words.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone in our family we need to say sorry to?”

illus: A shopkeeper in Mavelikara kept Moonnu Nombu strictly every year. One year his parish priest asked him whether he also paid his workers fairly. That year he raised their wages before the fast began. He said: Nineveh's king did not only fast; he told people to take the violence out of their hands.

pm.open: Lord, keep us awake for your coming, and let our fasting turn us from evil. Amen.
share: All shall turn from their evil ways (Jonah 3:8). What must I turn from?
Keep awake therefore (Matthew 24:42). Am I spiritually asleep?
Let love be genuine (Romans 12:9). Is my love sincere?
interc: For true conversion during the Three Days' Fast.
For an end to violence in our land.
For monks and all who pray for the world, through Mar Macarios, and for Geevarghese Mar Makarios on his name day.
pm.close: Father, give us watchful hearts, clean hands and genuine love as we wait for your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, on the second day of the fast Jonah obeys. He enters Nineveh and cries out. And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth (Jonah 3:5).

The king commands: all shall turn from their evil ways and from the violence that is in their hands (Jonah 3:8). Nineveh fasted with its hands as well as its stomach. Our fast too must change how we treat others.
Jesus warns that his coming will be like the days of Noah, when people did not notice until the flood came. Keep awake therefore, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming (Matthew 24:42).

Paul tells us how the watchful live: let love be genuine; rejoice in hope, be patient in suffering, persevere in prayer (Romans 12:9, 12). With Mar Macarios, let us keep the faith and keep awake. Amen.
kids: Children, the people of Nineveh stopped doing bad things and said sorry to God. Let us be kind at home today, and say sorry if we hurt someone.

intro: Nineveh's turning, the watchful heart, and genuine love.

q: Yet even now, says the LORD, return to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning; rend your hearts and not your clothing.
Let love be genuine; hate what is evil, hold fast to what is good;
points.apply: Put right one injustice this week.

q: Noah did this; he did all that God commanded him.
Keep awake therefore, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.
points.apply: Examine your conscience each night of the fast.

q: Seek the LORD while he may be found, call upon him while he is near;
Rejoice in hope, be patient in suffering, persevere in prayer.
points.apply: Pray the evening prayer with your family.

concl: A true fast turns us from evil.
The watchful live in genuine love and prayer.
2027-01-19.resolve: Make peace with one person before the fast ends.
